prompt: Against the standard-v3 table (sythis-enchantress / jarad-graveyard / abaddon) zur wins 4 of 47 decided games while edgar-vampires, ur-dragon and gishath sit at 0.33-0.41 and heliod at 0.28. The logs say how: sythis-enchantress deals 88 combat damage a game to zur's 16, eliminated zur in 20 of its 34 deaths, and zur dies by damage on median global turn 37; sythis wins every one of its 31 games by 'all opponents have lost'. Edgar beats the same seat by killing it first (64 combat damage a game, sythis dead in 28 of 46 games by median global turn 35). Zur has six interaction and fort pieces in total (Swords, Path, Imprisoned in the Moon, Sphere of Safety, Vito, Enduring Tenacity) and deck-audit reads interaction-breadth under target. Ownership is NOT a constraint: the pilot wants the absolute best list. What changes get zur to the fleet's 0.30 at this table -- a clock that does not have to attack through a fort, answers to a voltron creature and to a board of enchantments, or defence -- and which of those does the evidence actually support?
reading: The premise is half wrong: deck-audit counts 10 interaction copies (at target, floor 8) and 11 answers in the engine's 'AN ANSWER' component, not six — what zur lacks is answers that work on THIS seat. The 59-game log names what kills zur (46 of 59 games, all 37 attributed deaths by damage, median global turn 37): Angel tokens from Sigil of the Empty Throne (293 combat damage over 70 hits), the aura'd Sythis (243), the aura'd and indestructible Heliod (236 over 25 hits) and Hallowed Haunting Spirits (140) — a wide flying token board plus two voltron bodies, and in the 21 of 59 games (36%) where Privileged Position resolved, every one of them is hexproof against the seven of zur's answers that target a permanent (three more are counters, which a hexproof grant does not stop); Sterling Grove (22 casts) shrouds only enchantments, so of the four killers it shields Heliod alone; the one untargeted answer to a permanent already on the battlefield, The Meathook Massacre, was cast twice in 59 games. Every fleet deck that clears 0.30 here kills with 54.8-71.0 combat damage a game against zur's 15.81, and zur's own four wins carried 40, 52, 76 and 228 — so the gap is a clock, and the clock the goldfish measured is a band, not a number: goldfish_metrics.json's commander_ability_band reads kill_by_8 ceiling 0.381 with Zur's animate firing whenever affordable and floor 0.219 with it switched off, 0.162 owed to the ability — and the Forge AI activated it 7 times in 59 games (the band's own note: fired in 5% of games), so Forge measured a list near the floor, which makes 4 of 47 (0.085, ci95 [0.034, 0.199]) a reading of the deck's triggered output with the activation half largely unpiloted. The evidence supports, in this order: untargeted answers to the creature board (Winds of Abandon, Aetherize), a TRIGGERED clock the AI can pilot (Sigil, Hallowed Haunting — the same two cards that kill zur from the other side), drain as reach rather than as the kill, and a cheaper fort than the 5-mana Sphere of Safety that landed in 7 of 59 games (Ghostly Prison, which no audit axis can count) (goldfish cumulative drain 16.774 by T10 against three 40-life opponents; drain-v2 is at 3 of 60 Forge games and says nothing yet); it does NOT support answers to a board of enchantments — zur runs 45 enchantment copies itself, so every enchantment sweep in the identity is symmetric and worse for zur, and the one one-sided mass answer in the identity I can name, Cyclonic Rift overloaded, is a Game Changer — as is Farewell, which is symmetric — so either takes a 3-GC deck to bracket 4 at a bracket-3 table. No single change is evidenced to close 0.085 to 0.30, and at n=60 the run's MDE is wider than the gap any one card can make; the honest expectation is that the ten below move combat damage dealt, damage taken and elimination turn, and only a 400-game run reads the rate.

gaps: The captain's log is empty: zero paper games, so log_entries_read is empty and nothing here rests on a pilot's takeaway. Every finding is Forge or the goldfish.

Zur's own 59 games have no committed record (the run was killed one game short); the figures quoted are re-derived from the logs with manamap.sim.parse.analyze_logs, the same code the five fleet records were built with, and are not in any tracked artifact. A future record from a completed run may differ by the missing game.

The goldfish sees none of the mechanism this question is about — no blockers, no fort, no hexproof, no opponent creatures — so of the ten adds it can measure only Sigil of the Empty Throne, Hallowed Haunting, Sanguine Bond, Mesa Enchantress and Blind Obedience, and even those it measures against an opponent who never taxes an attack. Winds of Abandon, Aetherize, Ghostly Prison, Authority of the Consuls and Suture Priest are Forge-only.

No candidate_pool.json and no deck_recon.json exist for this deck; every add was verified against cards.csv with card-search (in identity, commander-legal, not in the 99) but none carries an inclusion rate. A recon pass would rank them against what Zur lists actually run.

The question asks what gets zur to 0.30. Nothing here is evidenced to move a win rate by 0.215; at n=60 the MDE against an 0.085 baseline is wider than any single card's effect, and the fleet's 0.33-0.41 comes with 55-71 combat damage a game that this list cannot produce while its kill is an activation the AI does not use. The measurable claim is narrower: these ten move combat_damage_dealt, combat_damage_taken and eliminated_turn, and a 400-game run reads the rate.
The interaction-breadth axis reads land uncovered; Field of Ruin answers a nonbasic land and the heuristic did not see it. Not a finding for this question either way.
